targets.title: Anticipatory control through associative learning of subliminal relations: Invisible may be better than visible.
targets.evidence_quote: We attempted to directly replicate Experiment 2 from Farooqui and Manly (2015), in which subliminal cues preceded task-switch and task-repeat trials in a standard task-switching paradigm.
targets.outcome_quote: The direct replication was unsuccessful: We found no evidence for effective subliminal cuing but observed some evidence for participants reducing switch costs with explicit, supraliminal cues.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall unsuccessful verdict, repeated in discussion. The four experiments independently manipulate cue visibility and knowledge; Experiment 1 directly replicates original Experiment 2 and Experiments 2–4 extend the test of the same published claim.

reasoning: Full primary manuscript including references; title and all four authors match. Completed new-participant experiments. Original Experiments 9 and 10 explain the motivation but are not explicitly specified as separate directly replicated protocols.
